item.name: Widget
item.description: The call that the widget script makes from the browser with the publishable key.

description.content: The widget script `pilgrim.js` calls this operation from the browser. It sends the publishable key of the client, not an API token. The operation finds or creates the contact and returns the URLs of the widget iframes. To prove the email of the contact, your server makes `user_hash`: the HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the trimmed, lowercase email, with the identity secret of the client as the key. Make the hash on your server only. Never put the identity secret in browser code. A wrong hash returns 403. A missing hash returns 403 when the client requires identity verification. Without a hash, the operation can create a new contact, but it does not update or sign in an existing contact. One IP address can create 20 contacts without a hash for each client each hour. After that, a call that creates a contact without a hash returns 429. The contact fields have limits: `email` must be an email of at most 255 characters, `name` at most 255 characters, `avatar` an http or https URL of at most 2048 characters, and `mrr` and `ltv` numbers from 0. The other fields of the contact are custom fields. They can have at most 50 keys, a depth of 3 and 16 KB, and no key can start with `pilgrim_`.

The Feedback Pilgrim API gives your code access to the posts, release notes, contacts, testimonials and tags of one client.

Each Feedback Pilgrim instance is self-hosted. The base URL is the `APP_URL` of your instance, for example `https://app.example.com`.

## Keys

The API uses two keys. Each operation names the key that it needs.

- **API token** (`apiToken`): a personal access token. Make one in **Settings → API Tokens**. The token belongs to one client. Each request reads and changes only the data of that client. Keep the token on your server.
- **Publishable key** (`publishableKey`): the `pk_` key of a client. The widget script `pilgrim.js` sends it to `POST /api/v1/init`. The key is public. It gives no access to the other operations.

Send the key in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. The API always answers in JSON. Send `Accept: application/json` with each request all the same, because it is the standard for a JSON API.

## Rate limits

Each user can make 120 requests each minute. All the tokens of one user share this limit. Requests without a user, such as widget `init` calls, count against the IP address. Each response has the headers `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. After the limit, the API returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

## Errors

An error response is JSON. Each error has a `message` field that says what went wrong. Some authentication errors of the widget and of the token check also have an `error` field, which older clients read. A `422` response also has an `errors` object with the messages for each field.

## Pagination

The list operations take `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 15). The response is a Laravel paginator: `data` holds the records, and `current_page`, `last_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `next_page_url` and the other fields describe the page.
